international.title: Badenoch says using amputee athletes to justify cutting disability benefits was ‘message of hope’ – UK politics live
international.summary: PM has asked Badenoch to withdraw her suggestion that benefits should be cut because ‘double amputees run marathons’ Alexandra Topping is a Guardian political correspondent. Kemi Badenoch was in a straight-talking mode on the media round this morning, calling the historic meeting between Trump, Xi and Putin “disturbing”, saying it looked like they were trying to “carve” up the world” between them. There are three world leaders who look like they’re trying to carve up the world between them, a tri-polar world where Xi gets Asia, America gets the western hemisphere and Russia gets Europe, and that is very concerning, especially seeing Donald Trump call President Putin his friend. Russia is not America’s friend, it certainly hasn’t been during my lifetime. But also at a time when we’re all worried about where the Ukraine war is going, the message that is sending to President Zelensky and of course the other summit that is taking place … is very concerning indeed. The thing that we need to do is continue to stand squarely by Ukraine and that is what this government will do. And on this issue, I do pay tribute to all sides of the house because that is what we’ve managed to do in the years since the conflict began and that is the right thing to do … Let that clear message go out as that meeting takes place in [China] – this country is squarely with Ukraine. I will speak the truth and I will say what I believe is common sense. And what I know is that, if people can work, then we should encourage them to work. And what I’m saying is actually a message of hope, that if people even with significant, problems can work, then those who have ADHD and mild anxiety should go to work. People are free to disagree, but they know where I’m coming from. I will post more from the interview shortly. Continue reading...
